results.title: The mitochondrial multi-omic response to exercise training ...
results.content: # Resource The mitochondrial multi-omic response to exercise training across rat tissues. Multi-omic atlas of the mitochondrial response to exercise training in 19 rat tissues. Robust temporal differences in mitochondrial response by -omes, tissues, and sex. Most dynamic responses in adrenal, brown adipose, colon, heart, liver, and muscle. Protein networks upregulated by exercise are downregulated in human T2D and cirrhosis. Here, the Molecular Transducers of Physical Activity Consortium mapped the temporal, multi-omic changes in mitochondrial analytes across 19 tissues in male and female rats trained for 1, 2, 4, or 8 weeks. Training elicited substantial changes in the adrenal gland, brown adipose, colon, heart, and skeletal muscle. The colon showed non-linear response dynamics, whereas mitochondrial pathways were downregulated in brown adipose and adrenal tissues. Exercise-upregulated networks were downregulated in human diabetes and cirrhosis. We provide a multi-omic, multi-tissue, temporal atlas of the mitochondrial response to exercise training and identify candidates linked to mitochondrial dysfunction.
